# Dastyare Social — CS

> Self-hosted, open-source creator studio. Publish text, image, video, voice, or file posts on your own server. No license required, built for both humans and AI agents.

> WARNING: SEO & LLM discovery is experimental. This site provides llms.txt, sitemaps, structured data, and MCP endpoints per current best practices, but whether search engines or AI assistants discover, cite, or surface its content can't be fully relied on.

Dastyare Social CS lets creators publish threads, shorts (vertical video), media posts, and ephemeral stories. External AI agents and LLMs should use the REST API documented below.

## Documentation

- [Interactive API docs (Scalar + MCP)](/docs): Full OpenAPI reference with try-it-out and MCP tool discovery
- [OpenAPI spec (JSON)](/openapi.json): Machine-readable API contract for tool use and code generation
- [AGENTS.md](/agents.md): Detailed agent guide with endpoint examples and auth flow
- [CONTEXT.md](/context.md): Compact project context — read this first for the quick answer

## API overview

Base URL: `{APP_URL}/api`

### Posts

- `GET /api/posts` — List posts (query: page, limit, search, type=list|count|shorts)
- `POST /api/posts` — Create post (JSON or multipart with file)
- `GET /api/posts/{id}` — Get single post
- `PATCH /api/posts/{id}` — Update post
- `DELETE /api/posts/{id}` — Delete post
- `POST /api/posts/{id}` — Actions: reaction, view
- `POST /api/posts` with `{ action: "batch-view", ids: [...] }` — Batch view increment

Post types: text, image, video, voice, file

### Stories

- `GET /api/stories` — List stories (query: page, limit, search, type=count, kind=image|video)
- `POST /api/stories` — Create story (JSON or multipart)
- `GET /api/stories/{id}` — Get single story
- `PATCH /api/stories/{id}` — Update story
- `DELETE /api/stories/{id}` — Delete story
- `POST /api/stories/{id}` — Actions: view, like (direction: inc|dec)

Story types: image, video

### Authentication

- Auth handler: `/api/auth/*` (Better Auth)
- Sign in: `POST /api/auth/sign-in/email`
- Bearer token or API key in `Authorization` header for protected operations
- Public GET endpoints do not require authentication

### Push notifications

- `POST /api/push` — Save a browser push subscription. Requires `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`.
- `POST /api/push/send` — Send browser push notifications to active subscribers. Requires `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`.
- Use this for self-hosted web push delivery to browsers that have enabled notifications.

### Webhooks

- `GET /api/webhooks` — List registered webhooks (with events and delivery status). Requires API key.
- `POST /api/webhooks` — Register a webhook: `{ "url": "...", "events": [...] }`. Requires API key. Returns the webhook with its secret (only shown once).
- `GET /api/webhooks/{id}` — Get a single webhook. Requires API key.
- `PATCH /api/webhooks/{id}` — Update URL/events/active. Requires API key.
- `DELETE /api/webhooks/{id}` — Delete a webhook. Requires API key.

Events: `post.created`, `post.updated`, `post.deleted`, `post.reacted`, `post.viewed`, `story.created`, `story.updated`, `story.deleted`, `story.viewed`, `story.liked`.

Deliveries are signed HTTP POSTs (`x-ds-webhook-signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256-hex>` over `t.<unix>.<rawBody>` using the webhook secret) with envelope `{ id, event, timestamp, data }`. Failed deliveries retry with backoff (up to 3 attempts); delivery status is tracked per webhook (`lastStatus`, `lastAttemptAt`, `failureCount`).

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

This app exposes an MCP server so AI agents can call posts/stories as tools instead of raw HTTP.

- Endpoint: `{APP_URL}/api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, JSON responses)
- Discovery: `{APP_URL}/.well-known/mcp` — returns an `mcpServers` manifest
- Guide: `{APP_URL}/docs` includes MCP tool documentation
- Tools: `list_posts`, `get_post`, `list_stories`, `get_story`, `count_stories`, `list_webhooks`, `get_webhook`, `get_resume_config` (public); `create_post`, `update_post`, `delete_post`, `create_story`, `update_story`, `delete_story`, `create_webhook`, `update_webhook`, `delete_webhook`, `update_resume_config`, `set_resume_enabled` (require `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`). Webhook tools manage the same endpoints as `GET/POST /api/webhooks` (`list_webhooks`, `get_webhook`, `create_webhook`, `update_webhook`, `delete_webhook`). Resume tools read/edit `config/about.config.yml` — the `/about` page reflects changes on the next request.

Connect a remote MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ds-cs": {
      "url": "{APP_URL}/api/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <API_KEY>" }
    }
  }
}
```

For a local stdio server against the database, run `bun run mcp` (write tools enabled when `MCP_API_KEY` or `API_KEY` is set).

## Optional

- tRPC endpoint at `/api/trpc` is for internal frontend use; external agents should use REST
- Content filtering (NSFW, HTML sanitization) applied on write paths
- Media uploads stored in S3-compatible object storage
- `/about` — the owner's about/resume page, active only when `enabled: true` in `config/about.config.yml`; indexable only when global indexing is also enabled. Agents can read and modify it via the `get_resume_config`, `update_resume_config`, and `set_resume_enabled` MCP tools.
